symptom.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by at least one fully syndromal manic episode, often with marked impairment in functioning, that may be accompanied by delusions or hallucinations congruent or incongruent with mood. Episodes typically develop over days to weeks, can last weeks to months if untreated, and may alternate with depressive episodes or periods of relative euthymia. Psychotic features usually emerge at the more severe end of mania, often involving grandiose or paranoid themes, and help distinguish it from hypomania in Bipolar II Disorder. Clinically, it must be differentiated from primary psychotic disorders and substance- or medication-induced conditions by the temporal relationship of mood and psychosis, the episodic course, family history, and response to mood stabilizers.

patient.personality: Zachary is a highly analytical, competitive professional who channels his intensity into data-driven problem solving, outdoor challenges, and a tendency to overthink every decision.
patient.stressor: In the months before onset, Zachary was promoted to a higher-stakes role at his bank just as the firm began restructuring its risk models in response to economic uncertainty, increasing scrutiny on his analyses and recommendations. Determined to prove himself, he started working very long hours, simultaneously maintaining his demanding fitness and outdoor routines and taking on a self-initiated machine-learning side project to outdo competing teams, leaving little room for rest or recovery. Gradually, his usual methodical style gave way to an increasingly scattered focus as he chased every new idea, toggling between work spreadsheets, personal trading schemes, and side coding projects, while becoming preoccupied with patterns he believed he alone could see in markets and daily events. After several months in which his productivity became erratic, he clashed with colleagues over grandiose proposals, missed critical deadlines, and made impulsive financial decisions that affected both his own investments and team outputs; his manager and a close friend intervened when he appeared unable to filter irrelevant from important information and strongly urged a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: “My mind keeps jumping to every little thing around me and I can’t stay focused on what I’m supposed to be doing.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I know it sounds out there, but for weeks I’ve been completely convinced that senior management and even the Fed are secretly watching my personal trades and emails because they’ve realized I’ve cracked some hidden pattern in the markets that no one else can see, and they’re trying to steal it from me before I change the whole financial system.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most days lately I’m either riding this intense high where I feel amped up and almost giddy, or I flip on a dime and snap at coworkers or my girlfriend over tiny things—like someone questioning a spreadsheet formula—because it feels like they’re getting in the way of something huge I’m trying to do.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: From the moment I wake up, I’m just buzzing with energy—jumping between going for long runs before dawn, hammering out new trading algorithms, rearranging my entire portfolio, and reorganizing the team’s models, and I don’t feel like I can sit still or slow down even when my body is exhausted.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I’ve gotten to this point where I genuinely believe I’m the only one in the firm who truly understands the risk models and that if people would just listen to me, I could not only save the bank but probably predict the next crash and become famous for revolutionizing how markets are priced.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: When I’m talking now, it’s like my mouth can’t keep up with my brain—I’ll start explaining an idea about a model, then veer into macroeconomics, then my trail running plan, and I just keep going without a break even when people are visibly overwhelmed or trying to cut in.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: I sit down to work on a report and within minutes I’m derailed by the ping of an email, a movement outside the window, a headline flashing on my phone, or even a pattern in the wallpaper, and I feel compelled to chase each one because they all seem weirdly important or connected.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: Over these past few months I’ve been cramming my days and nights with back-to-back meetings I schedule myself, extra analyses nobody asked for, late-night coding, nonstop networking coffees, and even ramped-up dating and sex, like I have to maximize every minute because I’m on the verge of some breakthrough.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.
S041.manifestation: I’ve started making huge, leveraged trades on my personal account, blowing through my savings and even taking out more credit, driving way too fast between the office and the gym, and hooking up with people I barely know, all because in the moment it feels completely safe and destined to pay off, even though a part of me knows it could all implode.
